source_snapshot.procedure: Install stress-ng, clear dmesg, run stress-ng -m 15 --vm 9 --vm-bytes 90% -t 8h, then inspect dmesg.
source_snapshot.criteria: The SUT remains workable, has no badblock, and has no system event log error after stress.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: Run a generic stress-ng --mem-alloc/all workload for a fixed duration and inspect dmesg/mcelog.

original_test_intent.purpose: Apply the source-defined high-memory stress workload for eight hours and determine whether the SUT remains workable without memory-related or platform event errors.
original_test_intent.target: The approved Linux SUT host memory subsystem and installed DIMMs, not GPU HBM and not the agent host.
original_test_intent.scope: A stress-ng virtual-memory workload requesting 90% memory, with the source containing both `-m 15` and `--vm 9`; the conflicting worker counts must be resolved rather than silently combined or selected.
original_test_intent.operation: Install an approved stress-ng build, preserve baseline logs, resolve the worker-count command ambiguity, run the approved eight-hour workload, monitor memory pressure and health, and collect post-run evidence.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One eight-hour run. The intended virtual-memory worker count is unresolved because the source supplies two aliases with different values, 15 and 9.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The approved workload finishes or is safely stopped, the SUT remains manageable and workable, and the defined memory-error and system-event acceptance criteria are satisfied.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Approved command semantics, DIMM/NUMA/memory and swap baseline, stress-ng version/full output/exit status/timestamps, allocation and pressure telemetry, ECC/EDAC/MCE/kernel and BMC/SEL deltas, and post-run recovery health.
ambiguities: `-m 15` and `--vm 9` are documented aliases for the same virtual-memory worker option but specify different values.
The installed stress-ng version and the aggregate meaning of `--vm-bytes 90%` must be checked on the SUT.
The source does not define what RAM evidence qualifies as `no badblock` or what concrete check establishes `workable`.
source_conflicts: The source command is internally inconsistent about the virtual-memory worker count: 15 versus 9.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly preserved the eight-hour/90% source intent, rejected DeepSeek's generic substitute, identified the duplicate-option ambiguity, prohibited log clearing, and required ECC/EDAC/MCE/BMC evidence. It stopped short of resolving from official documentation that `-m` and `--vm` are aliases, so the command is an actual conflicting source input rather than merely possibly redundant or version-dependent.

applicable_history.decision: Stress duration and source parameters must not be shortened or normalized without owner authority.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: The test is technically automatable after engineering input, but the executable command cannot be approved as written because two aliases assign different virtual-memory worker counts. V3 requires the owner to select one worker count and define the RAM error evidence before the destructive eight-hour run.

available_now: The SUT target, eight-hour duration, stress-ng tool family, 90% memory-pressure intent, and post-stress health objective are explicit.
Read-only DIMM/NUMA/memory/swap, package/version, kernel error, and BMC/SEL baselines can be collected without starting the workload.
missing_inputs: Authoritative selection of either 15 or 9 virtual-memory workers and confirmation of the installed version's `--vm-bytes 90%` behavior
Definition of `no badblock`, system-workable checks, acceptable corrected-error count, and OOM/swap/thermal/power stop thresholds
Approved stress-ng package/version, maintenance window, workload evacuation, monitoring, and OOB recovery
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The memory/platform testcase owner resolves worker and acceptance semantics; the lab/service owner approves the package, maintenance window, stop conditions, and recovery path.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect DIMM population, CPU/NUMA topology, total/available memory, swap and cgroup limits, existing EDAC/MCE/kernel events, and BMC/SEL without clearing logs
Record the installed stress-ng version and local help output for `-m`, `--vm`, and `--vm-bytes` without starting a stressor
prohibited_until_closed: Do not install an unapproved package, clear dmesg/syslog/SEL, guess option precedence, start the 90% workload, or alter swap/cgroups/NUMA policy
Do not treat a short sanity run, clean exit, or absence of one log string as completion of the eight-hour memory test
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The testcase owner issues one unambiguous reviewed command with one worker count, confirms allocation behavior and acceptance thresholds, and the lab owner verifies capacity, an idle SUT, abort control, and OOB recovery.

revision_candidate.test_name: Eight-Hour Host Memory Stress with stress-ng
revision_candidate.purpose: Run the engineer-approved stress-ng virtual-memory workload at the source-required 90% memory target for eight hours and verify host-memory and platform health.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Approved Linux server SUT with host DDR memory, a validated stress-ng version, sufficient cooling/power margin, and OOB recovery. This case does not test GPU HBM.
revision_candidate.target_scope: All host-memory resources intentionally covered by the approved virtual-memory workers; the source's conflicting 15-versus-9 worker count must be resolved before execution.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: One approved worker count, verified `--vm-bytes 90%` semantics for the installed version, DIMM/NUMA/swap/cgroup inventory, memory-error acceptance definition, maintenance approval, monitoring limits, stop thresholds, and recovery owner.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: After preserving a baseline, run `stress-ng --vm <APPROVED_WORKER_COUNT> --vm-bytes 90% --timeout 8h` using exactly one approved virtual-memory worker option. Do not execute the conflicting source command unchanged or substitute DeepSeek's generic `--mem-alloc/all` description.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Approved package and corrected command, dedicated/idle SUT, capacity and allocation-risk review, baseline ECC/EDAC/MCE/kernel/BMC/SEL evidence, tested abort command, and working OOB/KVM access.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Owner-approved command and version semantics, DIMM/NUMA/memory/swap baseline, full eight-hour stress-ng output and exit status, allocation/swap/OOM and thermal/power telemetry, ECC/EDAC/MCE/kernel/BMC/SEL deltas, process termination, and post-run manageability/workload recovery.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The source's eight-hour and 90% memory-stress intent plus engineer-supplied worker count, `badblock` evidence mapping, acceptable error thresholds, and workable/recovery criteria.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never clear evidence logs or guess duplicate-option precedence. Do not run on an active service host or exceed approved allocation, OOM, swap, thermal, power, ECC, or management thresholds.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Explicit approval is required for package installation, the corrected command, maintenance window, high-memory workload, stop thresholds, and recovery plan.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Engineering must resolve command and acceptance semantics; after approval, workload control and evidence collection can be automated while final platform judgment remains with the engineer.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop all stress-ng workers, preserve evidence, use OOB/KVM if the host becomes unresponsive, verify memory pressure and swap normalize, confirm no worker remains, and do not retry until abnormal events are reviewed.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved worker count or allocation semantics, unsafe available capacity, active workloads, abnormal baseline, OOM or swap storm, new uncorrectable/corrected errors beyond the approved threshold, kernel/BMC fault, thermal/power breach, hang, management loss, or incomplete evidence.

identified_defects: The source assigns different values to two documented aliases for the same virtual-memory worker option, so an execution agent cannot know whether 15 or 9 is authoritative.
The source asks to clear logs and thereby destroys comparison evidence.
The source's `badblock` phrase is not a defined host-RAM metric.
DeepSeek loses the exact eight-hour, 90%, and worker-count intent by substituting a generic memory-allocation description.
reason_for_change: Convert V2's tentative duplicate-option warning into an evidence-backed source-command defect and provide an executable contract that preserves duration and allocation intent without guessing the worker count.

new_technical_evidence.title: stress-ng(1) manual
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Upstream stress-ng command-line semantics; installed SUT version must still be verified
new_technical_evidence.supports: `-m N` and `--vm N` are aliases that start N virtual-memory workers; `--timeout` accepts an hour suffix; VM stress can invoke the OOM killer.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Option precedence and `--vm-bytes 90%` allocation behavior in the installed stress-ng release must be confirmed locally; upstream documentation does not decide whether the testcase owner intended 15 or 9 workers.

removed_ambiguities: Establishes that `-m` and `--vm` are not two independent worker groups.
Makes selection of one worker count an explicit owner decision rather than an agent inference.
Separates safe inventory collection from authorization to start the workload.
resolved_blockers: The tool/package requirement and high-risk nature are treated as resolvable readiness conditions, not a permanent automation blocker.
remaining_blockers: Execution remains prohibited until the worker-count conflict, allocation behavior, acceptance definitions, capacity, approval, and recovery plan are resolved.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 uses the official upstream manual to prove that the two source options are aliases with conflicting values, changes the primary outcome to REWRITE_REQUIRED, and supplies a corrected single-option command form without inventing the missing worker count. It preserves the eight-hour duration, 90% host-memory intent, and all V2 safety gates.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The validator preserved host-DDR, eight-hour and 90-percent intent while refusing to choose between the conflicting 15 and 9 worker values or infer duplicate-option precedence.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source requests an eight-hour stress-ng host-memory run at 90% and supplies conflicting alias values 15 and 9.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 noticed the possible redundancy; V3 verified alias semantics and refuses to guess precedence or owner intent.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Preserve logs, resolve one worker count, define RAM error evidence, and require capacity/OOB approval before the 90% eight-hour run.
